notes: Perfect match on three-color FRET experiments (C55-C60). Both evaluators find the evidence for sliding from anti-correlated acceptor intensities strong and convincing.

Complete match on rate enhancement claims (C8, C90-C92). LLM expresses uncertainty due to unknown binding probability parameters, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the modeling predictions as part of the significant advance, not questioning these computational claims.

Perfect match on dsDNA flipping controls (C95-C96). LLM finds the control experiments conclusive, while peer reviewers request additional statistical analysis of orientation fractions to confirm the conclusion.

High overlap on off-axis motion claims (C93-C94). LLM accepts that on-axis motion dominates based on DNA length dependence, while peer reviewers request additional discussion and potentially more data on how off-axis motion affects interpretations.

Substantial overlap on homology detection during sliding (C5, C9, C63-C68 shared). LLM finds the evidence for homology recognition convincing, while peer reviewers question whether transitions between HS1 and HS2 are definitively due to sliding given the short 5-nucleotide spacing, requesting discussion of alternative mechanisms.

Partial overlap on sliding model evidence (C47-C51 shared). Both evaluators find the evidence for sliding strong, particularly the linear dependence of cross-correlation time on filament length. Peer reviewers note this as especially convincing in Figures 2 and 3.

Moderate overlap on homology recognition efficiency (C10, C79-C84 shared). LLM finds the HMM/TDP quantitative analysis rigorous. Peer reviewers accept the data quality but question the mechanistic interpretation of transitions, creating uncertainty about the underlying mechanism rather than the measurements themselves.

Partial overlap on kinetic analysis claims (C71-C76 shared). Both evaluators accept the experimental design, discrete FRET states, and kinetic measurements. Peer reviewers' concerns are about mechanistic interpretation (addressed in R4), not the data quality itself.

Minimal overlap on diffusion coefficient estimates (C6-C7 shared). Both evaluators accept these quantitative estimates as supported by the experimental data, though peer reviewers request discussion of off-axis motion contributions to interpretation.

Minimal overlap (only C4 shared) on dynamic interactions. Both find evidence supported, but LLM result covers broader claim set (C4, C31-C41, C115-C118) about electrostatic interactions and FRET fluctuations, while peer result focuses on sliding evidence.
DNA melting control experiments (C42-C44) only evaluated by LLM. No corresponding peer review assessment found. LLM finds the control conclusive.
